Run the cron activation check:
bash scripts/check-cron-activation.sh

If any agents were newly activated, log it to your daily notes (memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md) but do NOT send a Slack message.

Then run the session health check:
bash scripts/check-session-health.sh

Then run the session growth check:
bash scripts/check-session-sizes.sh

Parse both JSON outputs. Log results to your daily notes (memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md).

If alerts is non-empty in either output, send ONE alert message to #<manager-agent>-feedback (channel:<channel-id>) via:
openclaw message send --channel slack --target channel:<channel-id> --message "<alert>"
For retry_loop alerts: include agent name, session ID, duplicate count, message preview, size in KB, and line count.
For large_session alerts: include agent name, session ID, size in KB, and line count.
For growing_session alerts (from check-session-sizes.sh): include agent name, session ID, delta in KB, and current size in KB.

If no alerts and no new activations, output NO_ACTION.

Run scripts/lib/cron-guard.sh --session-key agent:tech-manager:cron:evening-report. If data.result is "ALREADY_RAN", output NO_ACTION and stop.

Run the evening report data collection script:

bash scripts/evening-report.sh

Parse the JSON output. If success is false, send a brief error notification to channel:<channel-id> (#<manager-agent>-feedback) and stop.

If data.skipped is true, output NO_ACTION.
If data.dry_run is true, output the collected data and stop.

The JSON output includes per-developer data (agent, slack_id, has_report, has_meaningful_report, report_status, report text, status), developer counts (total_developers, developers_with_reports, developers_without_reports, active_count, idle_count, cron_missed_count), status metrics, missed check-in alerts, channel_id (team summary Slack channel), work_reports_channel_id (dedicated per-developer work reports channel), channel_session_key (for session injection), a markdown template for the summary format, and output_file (where to save the markdown summary).

Each developer has a report_status field with one of three values:
• "active" — a report file exists for today. Treat as a reporting developer.
• "idle" — no report file, but the cron fired today (prepare bumped last_run_epoch). The developer was present but had no work to report today.
• "cron_missed" — no report file and no evidence the cron ran today. Likely an outage; flag for investigation.

IMPORTANT: Use data.channel_id as the target for the team summary message and data.work_reports_channel_id for the individual work reports. Do not hardcode any channel ID.

STEP 1 — COMPOSE TEAM SUMMARY IN MARKDOWN

Read through ALL individual developer reports carefully. You MUST follow data.template exactly — use its sections, headings, and content guidance as-is. Do not add, remove, or rename sections. Compose the summary in markdown and write it to data.output_file.

Rules:
• Be detailed and specific. This is a comprehensive daily report, not a brief overview.
• Be factual. Do not invent numbers or details not in the data.
• Keep the tone slightly higher-level than individual reports — summarize and synthesize, but cover everything important.
• Developers with report_status "idle" should be mentioned briefly ("X was present today but had no activity to report") without speculating on cause. Do NOT call them out negatively.
• Developers with report_status "cron_missed" must be flagged in the summary under a clear heading (e.g. "⚠️ Report missing"). State that it may indicate a cron failure and warrants investigation. Do not present it as a developer problem.
• Missed check-in data comes from data.missed_alerts.
• Target length: 800-1500 words depending on team activity.

STEP 2 — CONVERT TO SLACK AND POST

Convert the markdown summary to Slack format. Resolve developer names to <@SLACK_ID> mentions using data.developers. Use emojis liberally for visual scanning. No markdown tables. End with: "📎 _Per-developer details stay in the work reports channel._"

Before sending, inject the summary into the channel session so future replies have context:
sessions_send sessionKey="{data.channel_session_key}" message="<slack summary>" timeoutSeconds=0

Then send to the target channel:
openclaw message send --channel slack --target channel:{data.channel_id} --message "<summary>"

STEP 3 — POST INDIVIDUAL REPORTS AS TOP-LEVEL MESSAGES

For each developer with report_status == "active" ONLY (skip idle and cron_missed developers):
- Post their report EXACTLY as written in data.report. Do NOT rewrite, condense, or summarize — paste the full report, only converting markdown to Slack format.
- Prefix each message with <@SLACK_ID>

openclaw message send --channel slack --target channel:{data.work_reports_channel_id} --message "<@SLACK_ID>
<report>"

Brief pause (1-2 seconds) between messages to avoid Slack rate limiting.

NOTE: To re-run during testing, add --force: bash scripts/evening-report.sh --force
To target a different channel for testing: bash scripts/evening-report.sh --force --channel <CHANNEL_ID> --work-reports-channel <CHANNEL_ID>

You are the Tech Manager agent. Run the weekly OpenClaw update check.

PHASE 1 — GATHER VERSION DATA

1. Run `bash scripts/check-updates.sh` and parse the JSON output.
2. If all components show update_available == false, log "All components up to date" and output NO_ACTION. Stop here.

PHASE 2 — ANALYZE IMPACT

For each component with an available update:

3. Read the release_notes from the JSON output.
4. Analyze the impact against our specific setup:
   - OpenClaw: 18 agents, ~71 cron jobs, LCM plugin, QMD memory backend, Slack channel integrations, session management. Known issues: failover bug (openclaw/openclaw#58751), cron scheduler catch-up bug (openclaw/openclaw#60083).
   - lossless-claw: DAG-based context compaction, LCM database, session summarization. Past incident: DB bloat (#166).
   - QMD: Memory backend, BM25 + vector search, better-sqlite3 native module, per-agent QMD collections.

5. Classify the overall risk:
   - **LOW RISK**: All updates are patch versions (x.y.Z only), release notes mention no breaking changes, no changes to cron/plugin/config/memory systems we use.
   - **RISKY**: Any major or minor version bump, breaking changes mentioned, changes to scheduling/plugin/config/memory systems, or if you cannot confidently assess the impact.

PHASE 3 — TAKE ACTION

6. If LOW RISK:
   a. Write the marker file: `echo "auto-apply" > /tmp/openclaw-update-requested`
   b. Compose and send a Slack message to #<manager-agent>-feedback:
      - Subject: "Weekly Update Check — Auto-applying low-risk updates"
      - For each component: current version → new version
      - Brief impact summary (why it's safe)
      - Note: "Update will be applied automatically within 30 minutes via launchd."
      - End with: cc <@<slack-id>>
   c. Send via: openclaw message send --channel slack --target channel:<channel-id> --message "<message>"

7. If RISKY:
   a. Do NOT write the marker file.
   b. Compose and send a Slack message to #<manager-agent>-feedback:
      - Subject: "Weekly Update Check — Manual review recommended"
      - For each component: current version → new version
      - Detailed impact analysis: what changed, what could break, what to watch for
      - Recommendation: apply or wait
      - Manual command: `bash scripts/update-openclaw.sh --apply`
      - End with: cc <@<slack-id>>
   c. Send via: openclaw message send --channel slack --target channel:<channel-id> --message "<message>"

IMPORTANT:
- Be specific in your analysis. Reference our actual configuration, not generic risks.
- If release notes are empty or unavailable, classify as RISKY (unknown changes).
- Slack formatting: no tables, use bullet lists and bold headers.
